subject: ventures/discogs-fee-calculator
professional: a high-volume Discogs record seller (US, thousands of orders a year) who reconciles payout statements; first checks: is the 9% applied to item plus shipping, the $0.10/$150 limits and what they apply to, whether the processing default matches what PayPal (Discogs' payment processor) actually takes, and whether a pasted crate prices every line correctly

evidence.correctness: Ran calc.mjs against hand computations (`node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/2d2e6a91-ab4e-5afb-9d66-7868d2f21338/scratchpad/dg/run.mjs`). $20 item + $6 shipping, $4.50 label, $5 cost: selling 0.09x26 = 2.34, processing 0.029x26+0.30 = 1.054, payout 18.106, profit 13.106: match. Same order at PayPal's published US PayPal Checkout rate 3.49% + $0.49 (paypal.com/us/business/paypal-business-fees, fetched): processing 1.3974: match. $2,500 grail: fee capped at 150, total 222.80, 8.912%: match. Target profit 20 on that order: 0.881c = 29.80, c = 33.8252, item price 27.8252: match. Payout target 2,000 across the cap: 0.971c = 2,150.30, c = 2,214.5211: match. $0.50 item hits the $0.10 floor: match. Not a 3: (1) the crate view, documented as ignoring '$ and thousands commas', silently turns 'Blue Note LP, $1,200.00' into item price $1 and shipping $200, and a bare '1,200' line into price 1 / shipping 200, with no problem reported (`node -e ... calculateBatch(...)`); (2) the processing default 2.9% + $0.30 matches none of PayPal's current published US rates (3.49% + $0.49 PayPal Checkout, 2.99% + $0.49 cards), and Discogs' own PayPal Payments Solution FAQ names PayPal as the processor, so a seller who leaves the default sees processing understated (on a $26 order 1.05 vs 1.40, 25% low; on a $3 single 0.39 vs 0.59). The $0.10/$150 limits could not be confirmed on a Discogs page: support.discogs.com returned 403 to WebFetch; Discogs' PayPal FAQ (search snippet) says min and max 'will be defined for each currency' without the numbers, and the one third-party source quoting $150 says 'per item', the tool says 'per order'.
evidence.completeness: README/page features checked by running: single-sale fee and payout (works), price for a target profit across the floor and cap (works), fee ladder $3 to $2,500 (feeLadder returns 9 rows), crate view with totals and losing count (works for plain numbers, misparses thousands commas as above), share links and where-to-sell handoff (share.test.mjs, to-where-to-sell.test.mjs pass), opt-out local usage counts (usage.mjs read, DNT/GPC honoured). Served copy clean: `node platform/pages/served-copy.mjs discogs-fee-calculator` -> no placeholder or retired origin. No stubs or TODOs found.
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/discogs-fee-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 51 tests, 51 pass, 485 ms. Six seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: SELLING_FEE_MIN 0.10 -> 0.05 SURVIVED (the floor test asserts sellingFeeOn(0.5) == SELLING_FEE_MIN, i.e. against the constant itself); small-order note threshold 5 -> 50 SURVIVED; processing on item instead of item+shipping caught; $150 cap -> 200 caught; default fixed 0.30 -> 0.49 caught; 4-cell label rule removed caught. No test feeds the crate a thousands-comma price, so the misparse is unguarded.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (264 lines), calc.test.mjs, index.html script, usage.mjs, share.mjs. Pure functions, one constants block, shared INPUT_IDS, DOM built with textContent (no injection), storage access guarded, bisection for the inverse is robust across the piecewise fee. Defects: batch parsing splits on every unquoted comma before stripping thousands separators, so the comment's promise cannot hold (calc.mjs:226-238); `discogsFee` names a sum that includes the payment processor's fee (calc.mjs:82), and the crate table heads it 'Discogs takes'.
evidence.claims: Backed by files and recomputation: 9% on item + buyer-paid shipping (Discogs PayPal Payments FAQ wording via search: 'charged on both the item price and the shipping costs'), 8% -> 9% on 2023-05-22 (Mixmag/Stereogum coverage of the Discogs notice), '$3 single ... about 22%' (21.9% run), '$2,500 ... about 9% all in' (8.9%), '$150 cap holds the selling fee to 6%' (6.0%), '$20 + $6 pays $2.34' and '$50 -> $43.75' (run), cap reached at ~$1,667 (1666.67). Disclaimer, not-affiliated line and privacy text on index.html:226-229, both SEO pages and README. Not backed: '$ and thousands commas are ignored' in the crate (calc.mjs:214-215, false for unquoted values); index.html:133 'Source: Discogs Help Center ... maximum of $150 per order. As of 2026-10-25' cannot be confirmed (page 403s; the only quote found says per item and Discogs says limits are per currency); 'third-party guides disagree' about processing (index.html:50/217) presents PayPal's own published rate as one rumour among three.
evidence.fitness: Job walked through: a US seller prices one sale, overwrites processing from a payout statement, reads payout, profit and the price for a target profit: works and is useful. Hit in the first hour: pasting a crate exported with thousands separators prices $1,200 records as $1 sales with $200 shipping, silently; leaving the processing boxes blank understates the PayPal fee; crate profit excludes postage (stated in the hint); non-USD sellers (per-currency min/max) and EU/UK sellers paying VAT on the selling fee are not modelled or mentioned; multi-item orders where Discogs' limits may apply per item are not modelled.
evidence.domain: Matches practice on the core: fee base includes buyer-paid shipping, floor and cap applied before processing, processing on the same total with a per-order fixed part, inverse solved numerically. Departures: the processing default is a Stripe-style 2.9% + $0.30 rather than the PayPal rate Discogs' processor publishes (3.49% + $0.49 PayPal Checkout in the US); USD-only limits although Discogs defines them per currency; no VAT on fees for UK/EU sellers; per-order vs per-item application of the limits unresolved and unflagged.

defects.what: Crate view silently misparses thousands-comma prices although the doc comment says '$ and thousands commas are ignored': 'Blue Note LP, $1,200.00' prices a $1 item with $200 shipping and '1,200' a $1 item with $200 shipping, with no problem reported. The split on unquoted commas happens before the separators are stripped.

Default processing 2.9% + $0.30 matches none of the rates PayPal (Discogs' processor per its PayPal Payments Solution FAQ) publishes for US sellers: 3.49% + $0.49 PayPal Checkout, 2.99% + $0.49 cards. A seller leaving the boxes blank sees processing about 25% low on a $26 order and a third low on a $3 single.

The $0.10/$150 limits are stated as 'per order' and sourced to the Discogs Help Center 'as of 2026-10-25', but Discogs' PayPal FAQ says limits are defined per currency and the only quote found says $150 'per item'; multi-item orders and non-USD sellers may be priced wrong and this is not flagged.

The $0.10 floor test compares sellingFeeOn(0.5) with the SELLING_FEE_MIN constant itself, so changing the constant to 0.05 leaves all 51 tests green; the small-order note threshold is also unpinned; no crate test uses a thousands separator.
VAT charged on the selling fee for UK/EU sellers (Discogs & Taxes FAQ) is neither modelled nor listed under 'What it does not know'.

Processing is presented as 'third-party guides disagree (2.7% + $0.25, 2.9% + $0.30, 3.49% + $0.49)' while PayPal publishes its rate; and the sum of selling fee and PayPal's fee is labelled 'Discogs takes' / discogsFee.

verdict: The single-sale arithmetic is right: five worked cases recomputed by hand (fee on item plus shipping, the $150 cap, the $0.10 floor, the price for a target profit on both sides of the cap, and the PayPal 3.49% + $0.49 rate typed in) match to four decimals, and every worked figure on the README and SEO pages checks out. It misses the bar on three counts. The crate view, documented as ignoring thousands commas, silently prices a '$1,200.00' record as a $1 sale with $200 shipping. The processing default 2.9% + $0.30 matches no rate PayPal, Discogs' processor, publishes for US sellers (3.49% + $0.49), so blank boxes understate the cut. And the '$150 per order' cap is cited to a Discogs page that could not be loaded, while the evidence found says limits are per currency and possibly per item. Tests are decent (51, four of six mutants caught) but the floor test checks the constant against itself.
